title: Dhruv Aggarwal
text: I am an experimental neuroscientist specializing in cognitive neuroscience and empirical memory research. I hold an MSc (Distinction) in Brain Sciences from the University of Glasgow. I am experienced in programming and executing controlled multifactorial cognitive experiments and eye-tracking paradigms. My research interests focus on mapping the neural bases for memory processes in the human brain. I am also an active advocate of open science practices such as preregistrations, preprints, and data sharing.

Involved in the development of the Trishul Research Program initiative - a collaborative research mentorship opportunity for high school and undergraduate students.
Responsible for auditing the program’s governing academic policy and compliance with international research standards while also coordinating with a multidisciplinary and international cohort of academic mentors.

title: Resources I Used
text:
As someone with a background in psychology and neuroscience, I was introduced to Quarto and R very recently. Since I had no prior experience, coding and data science seemed extremely complex and intimidating.
Thankfully, I have had the chance to use some amazing open-science materials posted across forums to learn. To make this website, I used the following guide made by Dr. James Bartlett at the University of Glasgow (UK): Dissemination using Quarto and Github Pages used under a CC-BY-SA-4.0 license.






Note



I shall update this page as and when I come across new Quarto resources worth sharing.
